stemMd: Which statement cannot be true in any permitted order?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Practice and Ethics must occupy consecutive positions, in either order.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Safety and Ethics must occupy consecutive positions, in either order.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Practice and Ethics must not occupy consecutive positions.

explanationMd:
Test whether each proposed statement can be added consistently to the rules. "Safety and Ethics must occupy consecutive positions, in either order." is incompatible with every permitted order. The alternative statements each have a complete valid example, given in their feedback. To check impossibility, enumerate placements for the most restricted item or block, then remove every case breaking a rule.

Complete permitted orders (each arrow advances one position):
- Access → Records → Safety → Practice → Ethics
- Access → Safety → Practice → Records → Ethics
- Ethics → Access → Safety → Records → Practice
- Ethics → Records → Access → Safety → Practice

independentSolve.workingNotes: Blind re-solve in the 5 November 2026 AI audit of this expansion (the review packet held no key, explanation or distractor notes; status "verified_key_agreement"; it checked for competing defensible answers and flagged none): Independently enumerated all 120 permutations of Access, Records, Safety, Ethics, Practice. Rules Safety must occur after Access and before Practice. Records must occupy position 2 or position 4. Ethics and Safety must not occupy consecutive positions. leave 4 valid orders: Access>Records>Safety>Practice>Ethics; Access>Safety>Practice>Records>Ethics; Ethics>Access>Safety>Records>Practice; Ethics>Records>Access>Safety>Practice. Choice true counts: a=3, b=0, c=2, d=1; impossible requires zero matches.
